messages:
mike: Heads up — CI nightly shows ~18% p50 small-batch latency regression on A100 after driver+torch bump. Trace points at a change in the prefetch cost model; attaching profiler snippets.
perf-ci-bot: Regression detected on build 3376543200 (nightly): smallseq p50 +18%, p95 +12%. Compare: https://perf.redwood/compare/3376543200
kate: ugh. which commit rolled with the bump? any obvious suspect merges?
raj: I pulled a flamegraph from the failing job — the estimator now calls buffer_create() per request which wasn't happening before. snippet:
```
// prefetch cost compute (simplified)
cost = (kv_bytes / bandwidth_est) + (kernel_launch_overhead * n_kernels)
if (cost < batch_threshold) prefetch();
```
The buffer_create path is hot.
lucy: @mike can you start a bisect between the last green driver job and this one? I'll gate the rollout until we have a cause.
mike: starting bisect. range: 3369000000..3376543210. quick pass narrows to PR #4789 (runtime): "prefetch cost-model refactor" — it changed batching cost calc and kernel prewarm order.
raj: Confirming locally: reverting #4789 restores p50. Minimal repro: `./scripts/bench smallseq --iterations 500 --device a100` shows ~14% p50 improvement after revert.
ci-bot: Repro run output:
BEFORE (with #4789): p50=12.3ms
AFTER (revert #4789): p50=10.7ms

kate: If it's that PR we should revert ASAP. Marking as rollout-blocker.
mike: opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812 (revert of #4789). tagging @eng-sre @eng-runtime.
raj: Also noticed more frequent kernel switching in the execution timeline (kernel A -> B per token). Looks like the new tie-breaker in the cost model moves affinity which causes extra kernel_launch overhead per step.
lucy: Is there a lower-risk patch? e.g., keep kernel affinity and avoid buffer_create churn, rather than full revert?
kate: I agree with the approach: revert to unblock rollout, then follow-up PR to rework estimator with perf tests.
mike: deploying revert to canary now.
perf-ci-bot: Canary job 3376543301 results: p50 returned to baseline. No regressions detected. Rolling revert to staging.
kate: Follow-up actions: add unit test to cover prefetch caching, add perf-guard in CI to compare smallbatch p50 vs baseline on A100.
raj: I'll open a follow-up PR to rework the estimator to preserve kernel affinity and avoid per-request buffer creation. Will include microbenchmarks. Ping me for review.
mike: Thanks all. Keeping the thread updated as rollout progresses. :thumbsup:
